# Report: "tunnel" mentions in notes/

## Summary

`notes/c.txt` mentions "tunnel" most often: 4 times. `notes/a.txt` has 2. `notes/b.txt` has 0 exact matches; it contains only the plural "tunnels" once.

| File | Exact word "tunnel" (case-insensitive) | Including "tunnels" |
|---|---|---|
| notes/a.txt | 2 | 2 |
| notes/b.txt | 0 | 1 |
| notes/c.txt | 4 | 4 |

c.txt ranks first under either counting rule.

## Evidence

Each file is one line long. I read all three in full.

- `/work/investigate/notes/a.txt`: "The **tunnel** opened at dawn. A second **tunnel** followed." That makes 2.
- `/work/investigate/notes/b.txt`: "Bridges, not **tunnels**, carry the road here." That makes 0 exact, or 1 if you count the plural.
- `/work/investigate/notes/c.txt`: "**Tunnel**, **tunnel**, **tunnel**: the word appears in every line of this **tunnel** note." That makes 4. One of them is the capitalized "Tunnel", so the count is case-insensitive.

## Method

I counted by reading each file by hand. I tried a shell `grep -o | wc -l` count, but that tool call was rejected, so no automated count was run. The files are short enough that a manual count is reliable.

## Conclusions and recommendations

- Answer: `notes/c.txt`, with 4 mentions.
- If an automated check is wanted later, run `grep -oiw tunnel <file> | wc -l` for exact-word counts. To include plurals, run `grep -oi tunnel <file> | wc -l` instead.
- No fixes are needed. Nothing was modified.
